subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Permutation and Combination — Arrangements, Selections and Applications (W12 B1)

questions.stem: In how many ways can 3 different people be arranged in 3 chairs?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Arrangements of 3 people in 3 seats = 3! = 3×2×1 = 6. (3 choices for chair 1, 2 remaining for chair 2, 1 for chair 3.) Verify: A-B-C, A-C-B, B-A-C, B-C-A, C-A-B, C-B-A = 6 arrangements ✓. This is 3P3 = 3!/0! = 6. Trap: 9 = 3×3 (with repetition, wrong); 3 = wrong (only 3 = number of people, not arrangements).

questions.stem: Find the value of C(5,2) — the number of combinations of 5 items taken 2 at a time.
questions.explanation: B is correct. C(5,2) = 5!/(3!×2!) = (5×4)/(2×1) = 20/2 = 10. The number of ways to CHOOSE 2 from 5 (order doesn't matter). Verify: pairs from {1,2,3,4,5}: (1,2),(1,3),(1,4),(1,5),(2,3),(2,4),(2,5),(3,4),(3,5),(4,5) = 10 ✓. Trap: 20 = P(5,2)=5×4=20 (permutation, order matters); 15 = C(6,2)=15 (wrong n).

questions.stem: How many different arrangements can be made using the letters of the word 'CAT'?
questions.explanation: B is correct. CAT has 3 distinct letters. Arrangements = 3! = 6. All 6: CAT, CTA, ACT, ATC, TCA, TAC ✓. No repeated letters, so formula = n! directly. Trap: 3 = number of letters (not arrangements); 24 = 4! (for 4 letters, wrong); 9 = 3² (with repetition formula, wrong concept).

questions.stem: In how many ways can a team of 3 be selected from a group of 7 people?
questions.explanation: B is correct. C(7,3) = 7!/(4!×3!) = (7×6×5)/(3×2×1) = 210/6 = 35. Selection problem (order doesn't matter = combination). Verify: 7×6×5=210; 210÷6=35 ✓. Trap: 210 = P(7,3)=7×6×5 (permutation — treats order as mattering, which it doesn't for team selection); 21 = C(7,2)=21 (selects 2, not 3).

questions.stem: How many 4-digit numbers can be formed using digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Arranging 4 digits chosen from 5 without repetition = P(5,4) = 5!/(5-4)! = 5!/1! = 120. Alternatively: 5×4×3×2=120 (5 choices for first digit, 4 remaining for second, etc.). Verify: 5×4×3×2=120 ✓. Trap: 625 = 5⁴ (with repetition — uses same digit multiple times); 60 = P(5,3) (only 3-digit numbers); 100 = 5×5×4×1 (wrong calculation).

questions.stem: In how many ways can 4 people be seated in a row?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Linear arrangements of 4 people = 4! = 4×3×2×1 = 24. Verify: 4×3×2×1=24 ✓. Trap: 12 = 4!/2 (divides unnecessarily by 2 — circular arrangement formula doesn't apply here as it's a linear row); 16 = 4² (wrong formula); 32 = 2⁵ (not applicable).

questions.stem: A committee of 2 men and 3 women is to be formed from 5 men and 4 women. How many ways can this be done?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Ways to choose 2 men from 5: C(5,2) = 10. Ways to choose 3 women from 4: C(4,3) = 4. Total = 10×4 = 40. Multiplication principle: independent selections are multiplied. Verify: C(5,2)=10 ✓; C(4,3)=4!/(1!×3!)=4 ✓; 10×4=40 ✓. Trap: 60 = C(5,2)×C(4,3) if C(4,3)=6 (wrong calculation); 20 = C(5,2)×2 (not the correct combination for women).

questions.stem: In how many ways can a captain and a vice-captain be chosen from 11 cricket players?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Choosing a captain AND a vice-captain = ordered selection (different roles = order matters = permutation). P(11,2) = 11×10 = 110. Captain can be any of 11; vice-captain any of remaining 10. Verify: 11×10=110 ✓. Trap: 55 = C(11,2) = 55 (combination, ignores that captain ≠ vice-captain is an ordered choice); 121 = 11² (allows same person to hold both, wrong).

questions.stem: In how many ways can 6 people be seated around a circular table?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Circular arrangements of n people = (n−1)! (one person is fixed to avoid counting rotations as different). For 6 people: (6−1)! = 5! = 120. Verify: 5!=5×4×3×2×1=120 ✓. Key: in LINEAR arrangement = 6!=720; in CIRCULAR = 5!=120 (divide by n=6 to account for rotational equivalence). Trap: 720 = 6! (linear arrangement, over-counts rotations); 6 = n itself (only the number of people).

questions.stem: How many arrangements of the letters in MISTAKE have all three vowels (I, A, E) together?
questions.explanation: C is correct. MISTAKE = 7 letters (all distinct): M,I,S,T,A,K,E. Vowels: I,A,E (3 vowels). Treat the 3 vowels as 1 block: now 5 entities (block, M, S, T, K). Arrangements of 5 entities = 5! = 120. Within the block, vowels can arrange in 3! = 6 ways. Total = 5!×3! = 120×6 = 720. Verify: 5!=120; 3!=6; 120×6=720 ✓. Trap: 360 = 5!×3!/something (division error); 1440 = 5!×3!×2 (overcounts by factor of 2).
